name: browser-use
headline: Vet - Malicious Package Detection
short_description: Vet detects malicious open source packages in real-time, integrating with software development workflows to enhance security. It benefits DevOps and security teams by preventing supply chain attacks, connecting to package managers like npm, PyPI, and RubyGems.
author: safedep

sections.overview:
Vet is a security tool that identifies malicious open source packages as they enter your development pipeline. It integrates directly with package managers including npm, PyPI, and RubyGems to scan dependencies before they're used in your codebase. The tool works by analyzing packages against known vulnerability and malware databases, helping teams prevent supply chain attacks at the source. Vet is designed for DevOps and security teams who need automated protection without disrupting their existing workflows. By catching compromised packages early, it reduces the risk of deploying vulnerable or malicious code to production.
Scan for malware in open source dependencies to prevent security breaches.
Integrate vet into CI/CD pipelines to automatically fail builds on critical vulnerabilities.
Define and enforce security policies using CEL expressions for tailored compliance.
Analyze specific packages for known vulnerabilities and malware before deployment.
sections.setup:
No install command available. Check the GitHub repository for manual installation instructions.
`git clone https://github.com/safedep/vet`
sections.usage:
```
Scan the [PACKAGE_MANAGER] project in [PROJECT_DIRECTORY] for malicious open source packages using Vet. Flag any packages with [SPECIFIC_RISK_LEVEL] or higher severity. Provide a detailed report including package names, versions, risk scores, and recommended remediation steps. Focus on dependencies that are [DIRECT_DEPENDENCIES/INDIRECT_DEPENDENCIES] and highlight any packages with known vulnerabilities from sources like [NVD/CVE_DATABASE].
```
